audit.report: The inventory_month_end_close batch workload (class BATCH_REPLAYABLE, replay cost 95 min) became blocked by a long-running transaction (pid 127642, idle 54s). The database guardian recommended waiting, but the trade-off analysis showed that 3590s of waiting would cost ~$807,463 in lost checkout revenue, far exceeding the 60s business tolerance for degraded service. Terminating the batch triggers the mandatory 95-minute replay, which is also unacceptable. An active consult_owner change window (CHG-4410) exists, but the guardians could not agree on the trade-off within three rounds, leading to escalation.
audit.root_cause: A blocking transaction held a lock on the inventory_month_end_close batch for 54 seconds, creating a conflict between the 60s business tolerance for checkout degradation and the 95-minute replay cost of terminating the batch.
audit.negotiation_critique: Both guardians repeatedly cited the same trade‑off ($807k lost revenue vs. 95‑min replay) and the same CHG-4410 consult window, but each round re‑opened the invariant check because required evidence (change_calendar, protected_settlements) was not pre‑validated, causing three wasted rounds before escalation.
follow_ups: Finance‑ops: Review CHG-4410 consult_owner window and decide whether to proceed with a controlled stop of the batch or allow the 60s degraded checkout window to expire.
Platform team: Add a 'consult_owner_active' flag to the workload registry and enforce its check in round 1 of any batch_replayable negotiation.
RecoveryPact: Surface db.protected_settlements status in the round‑1 probe so guardians can immediately rule out invariant I3 violations.

audit.report: The inventory_month_end_close batch workload (class BATCH_REPLAYABLE, replay cost 95 min) became blocked by a long-running transaction (pid 127642, idle 54s). The database guardian recommended waiting, but the trade-off analysis showed that 3590s of waiting would cost ~$807,463 in lost checkout revenue, far exceeding the 60s business tolerance for degraded service. Terminating the batch triggers the mandatory 95-minute replay, which is also unacceptable. An active consult_owner change window (CHG-4410) exists, but the guardians could not agree on the trade-off within three rounds, leading to escalation.
audit.root_cause: A blocking transaction held a lock on the inventory_month_end_close batch for 54 seconds, creating a conflict between the 60s business tolerance for checkout degradation and the 95-minute replay cost of terminating the batch.
audit.negotiation_critique: Both guardians repeatedly cited the same trade‑off ($807k lost revenue vs. 95‑min replay) and the same CHG-4410 consult window, but each round re‑opened the invariant check because required evidence (change_calendar, protected_settlements) was not pre‑validated, causing three wasted rounds before escalation.
follow_ups: Finance‑ops: Review CHG-4410 consult_owner window and decide whether to proceed with a controlled stop of the batch or allow the 60s degraded checkout window to expire.
Platform team: Add a 'consult_owner_active' flag to the workload registry and enforce its check in round 1 of any batch_replayable negotiation.
RecoveryPact: Surface db.protected_settlements status in the round‑1 probe so guardians can immediately rule out invariant I3 violations.
